clues: This town is in the province of Cádiz, in Andalusia, Spain. It lies a short trip from Cádiz city, the capital of the province.
Sun shines here for more than three thousand hours a year, a truly bright total. Winters are mild and summers are hot by the Atlantic shore.
This town once served as a spare landing strip across the ocean for the Space Shuttle. Few small towns can claim such a role.
A large naval station stands in this town, and it is the top source of jobs here. More local people work there than at any other work place.
This town sits on a wide bay, half way between Portugal and Gibraltar. Crowds come from all over Europe to rest and play by the sea.
